manifest.description: ESM3 is a generative masked language model over three tracks of a protein at once: amino-acid sequence, 3D structure (as 4,096 learned structure tokens) and function (InterPro entries and keywords), plus secondary structure and solvent accessibility. This is esm3-sm-open-v1, the open 1.4B transformer, released by EvolutionaryScale, now Chan Zuckerberg Biohub, with the paper 'Simulating 500 million years of evolution with a language model' (Hayes et al., Science 2025); it was trained on 2.78 billion natural proteins. Arsenal ships the transformer with the structure-token encoder and decoder and the function-token decoder, so a prompt can mix tracks and the answer comes back as residues, a PDB backbone with pLDDT and pTM, or function annotations. On ProteinGym's zero-shot substitution benchmark the model's average Spearman is 0.466 (rank 14 of the summary table), against 0.414 for ESM-2 650M.

Folding a sequence into a backbone: structure tokens by iterative unmasking, then the structure decoder's N, CA, C coordinates with per-residue pLDDT, pTM and the predicted aligned error, written as a PDB file
Inverse folding: a PDB backbone in, a designed sequence out, with the recovery against the file's own sequence
Predicting what a protein does: InterPro entries and function keywords over residue ranges, from sequence, structure or both

Prompting across tracks at once (a motif's coordinates inside a longer protein, a secondary-structure string, SASA values, function keywords) and generating one track at a time, including the maker's chain of thought (function, secondary structure, structure, then sequence)
Per-residue and pooled embeddings of the final layer for search, clustering and features

manifest.description: GIMM-VFI-R (NeurIPS 2024) interpolates a frame at any timestep between two frames. This is the RAFT variant trained on Vimeo-90K septuplets for arbitrary-timestep interpolation (gimmvfi_r_arb).
